saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint uses HTTP 200 even when the SAML response indicates an authentication or protocol error.
saml.note: Test oracles must inspect SAML StatusCode/content, not just HTTP status.

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow.
saml.note: IdP-initiated attempts failing are by design and not a flow-coherence bug.

saml.description: Token introspection reports active only when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: An inactive result can be expected even for valid tokens if the introspecting client is not in audience.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token, the returned token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This looks odd but follows RFC 8693 behavior as implemented by ZITADEL.

saml.description: Token exchange may return a scope different from the requested scope because ZITADEL validates and computes the final scope.
saml.note: A scope mismatch alone is not evidence of escalation or denial; compare against policy and upstream authorization.

saml.description: Introspection only reports active=true when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: Inactive introspection from the wrong client is expected and should not be treated as token invalidation.

saml.description: ZITADEL uses opaque access tokens by default unless an application is configured for JWT auth token type.
saml.note: Tests must not assume every access token is a JWT.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when the SAML response contains an error status.
saml.note: Tests must inspect SAML StatusCode/content, not just HTTP status.

saml.description: Userinfo and introspection only return claims permitted by granted scopes; many fields are omitted unless explicitly requested.
saml.note: Missing email, profile, metadata, or roles is not a bug if the scope was not requested.

saml.description: External IdP logins may automatically create or link accounts depending on provider settings such as automatic creation, manual creation allowed, manual linking allowed, and automatic linking options.
saml.note: Identity merges under enabled linking/creation settings can be by design.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. Do NOT attempt IdP-initiated SAML tests against ZITADEL as broker/SP behavior; they are unsupported by design and will produce false positives for I3/I1.

For all SAML login tests, the executor MUST first initiate the SP flow at /saml/v2/SSO and preserve the resulting request state. ZITADEL's SAML flow is request-bound and the response must match the original request (including InResponseTo semantics in normal SAML processing). Sending a standalone fabricated response without flow initiation will be rejected for the wrong reason.

The /saml/v2/SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on SAML protocol errors; failure is conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode/message, not the HTTP status. Do NOT treat HTTP 200 as login success for SAML tests. Parse the SAML response content to distinguish protocol failure from successful authentication.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-security testing, create the SAML provider with only metadata/default template settings and do NOT add extra hardening beyond documented defaults. The test is specifically whether default trust/signature validation is secure; adding validation options would invalidate the test.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch testing, issuer trust comes from exchanged metadata/entity IDs. The fuzzer MUST vary the assertion Issuer/idp_entity_id while keeping the configured provider fixed. If the provider was created from attacker-controlled metadata matching the forged issuer, the test is invalid because trust was explicitly configured to that issuer.

For I1/I5 SAML audience and conditions tests, ZITADEL documentation states the ACS/SP must validate destination, audience, recipient, issuer, signatures, validity window, and duplicate IDs as best practices. A valid negative test must mutate exactly one of these dimensions at a time; combining wrong audience with missing conditions or signature changes makes root-cause attribution impossible.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay, use the SAME assertion identifier across both submissions. ZITADEL documentation explicitly recommends historical cache / duplicate ID rejection as SAML best practice, so replay tests are only meaningful when the assertion ID is fixed across attempts.

For I2 freshness tests on OIDC/JWT-based downstream tokens, include a control token exchange or code exchange using a valid token alongside the attack case. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED or inactive introspection cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication, wrong audience, or misconfigured application settings.

JWT client assertions used for token or introspection authentication MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain and iat not older than 1 hour. Tokens outside this window fail for client-auth reasons, which would confound I1/I2 tests unrelated to the subject token or SAML assertion under test.

Token exchange audience narrowing is enforced: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and cross-org tests, ensure the attack audience is outside that combined set; otherwise acceptance is by design.

Token exchange scope behavior is not simple intersection. ZITADEL documentation says requested scope can be entirely different from supplied token scope and may extend or decrease it, subject to validation. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's actual returned scope/claims against upstream authorization intent and broker policy rather than assuming omission means inheritance or request means grant.

When requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. Do NOT use that returned access_token as a Bearer token for verify_granted_identity or resource access; doing so causes false failures unrelated to authorization binding.

ZITADEL introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. For verification, the fuzzer MUST introspect with a client/application that is in the token audience. Otherwise active=false is expected by design and must not be flagged as revocation or freshness failure.

Reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization. In multi-tenant SAML/OIDC broker tests, include or omit this scope intentionally. Unexpected login failure with this scope may be due to org-membership enforcement, not SAML validation.

Reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds that project to the access-token audience. For I5 audience-binding tests, explicitly request or withhold these scopes to control audience. ZITADEL's default audience already includes client IDs and the project ID of the application, so tests must account for these built-in audiences before claiming overbroad audience acceptance.

ZITADEL supports opaque access tokens by default. Resource-server style verification should prefer introspection, not local JWT parsing, unless the application is explicitly configured for JWT auth token type. Misclassifying an opaque token as malformed JWT is a test setup error, not an I1/I2 failure.

For SAML brokered user creation in Login V2, required user fields may need to be mapped from IdP attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. If these mappings are absent, first-time SAML login can fail because user creation data is incomplete, which is not evidence of secure rejection of the SAML assertion.

SAML attribute names and NameID values are provider-specific and may be mapped into ZITADEL user fields by actions. For I4 collision tests such as saml_email_binding_collision, verify whether account linking/creation logic is using email, username, or IdP link fields configured by actions before interpreting a merge as a broker bug.

External IdP login must be enabled in the login policy before SAML provider tests. If external login is disabled, SAML authentication paths are blocked by policy and any login failure is non-security-related setup failure.
ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. Do NOT attempt IdP-initiated SAML tests against ZITADEL as the broker/SP side; such failures are by design and not security findings.

For SAML broker tests, the executor MUST first initiate the SP flow and preserve request state. ZITADEL's SAML flow starts at /saml/v2/SSO and the resulting SAMLResponse is tied to the original request/RelayState; fabricated standalone responses without the initiated flow context will be rejected for the wrong reason.

The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on authentication errors; failure details are carried inside the SAML StatusCode/message, not the HTTP status. Do NOT treat HTTP 200 from /saml/v2/SSO as success in I1/I2/I5 tests.

For SAML IdP-brokering setup in ZITADEL Login V2, user creation will fail unless required user fields are mapped from IdP attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. A failed first-login due to missing mapped attributes is setup failure, not proof that a forged assertion was rejected.

When testing SAML issuer validation (saml_issuer_mismatch), configure the SAML provider with imported metadata or explicit IdP entity ID from the upstream IdP. If provider trust is not fully configured from metadata, issuer mismatch results are uninterpretable because trust anchors may be incomplete.

For SAML audience-binding tests, use the ZITADEL SP entity ID exactly as documented by the provider details/metadata URL. Guides consistently map downstream IdP 'Audience / SP Entity ID / Identifier' to the ZITADEL Metadata URL; a wrong audience should be compared against that exact value.

External IdP login is gated by login policy. Before any SAML broker login test, enable 'External Login allowed' on the instance or organization login policy; otherwise login failures are policy denials, not SAML validation outcomes.

If organization-specific settings override defaults, the auth request MUST include the reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may use default instance settings and the wrong IdP/login policy, causing false positives or false negatives in SAML tests.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Requests outside that combined set are expected to fail by design and should not be reported as a broker bug.

For I5 token-exchange scope escalation tests, ZITADEL documentation explicitly allows requested scope to differ from supplied token scope and says it can be used to extend or decrease scope, with server-side validation determining the final scope. Do NOT assume any scope increase is automatically a vulnerability; verify whether the exchanged token actually exceeds upstream authorization plus ZITADEL policy.

For I5 token-exchange subject-token audience tests, the introspection endpoint reports active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. A false/401 introspection result from the wrong client is expected audience enforcement, not token invalidity.

For I2 freshness tests on JWT profile or private_key_jwt client assertions, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Use control assertions with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}; otherwise rejection may be due to malformed client authentication rather than the freshness condition under test.

ZITADEL does not support the OAuth 2.0 SAML 2.0 bearer grant. Do NOT model SAML broker login as a direct token-endpoint SAML assertion grant; SAML in the supplied docs is browser-based federation, while /oauth/v2/token supports authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, jwt-bearer, and token-exchange.

When requesting user identity claims for verification, include the necessary scopes. UserInfo and introspection return claims depending on granted scopes; missing email/profile/roles claims after login is expected if those scopes were not requested.

Token exchange with requested_token_type=id_token returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A. Do NOT use that returned access_token as a Bearer token for verify_granted_identity or resource access; it is not an API credential.

For SAML broker login tests, the fuzzer MUST initiate the browser/OIDC flow first and then drive the SAML exchange through the external IdP path. ZITADEL acts as the broker and completes login by returning to OIDC endpoints; testing only /saml/v2/SSO without the surrounding auth flow can misinterpret broker behavior.

SAML login failures at /saml/v2/SSO may still return HTTP 200 with an error encoded in SAML StatusCode/message. Do NOT treat HTTP 200 as success for SAML tests; parse the SAML response status to distinguish acceptance from rejection.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-security tests, create the SAML provider with only metadata/default template settings and do NOT add extra hardening assumptions not documented in the provider config. The docs emphasize metadata-driven configuration; acceptance under default setup is the relevant signal.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, issuer trust is derived from exchanged metadata. The fuzzer MUST configure the provider from metadata URL/XML first; otherwise an issuer mismatch result is uninterpretable because no trust anchor was established.

For I5 saml_wrong_audience and saml_no_audience_restriction tests, use the ZITADEL SP entity ID/metadata URL as the expected audience because the guides repeatedly instruct upstream IdPs to set Audience/SP Entity ID to the ZITADEL Metadata URL. Any other audience should be rejected.

For I5 saml_no_conditions tests, a successful broker login may still fail later if user creation fields are missing. Configure the documented Actions V2 response manipulation to map required SAML attributes (email, first/last name, username/IdP link) before interpreting acceptance of malformed assertions; otherwise failures may be due to provisioning, not assertion validation.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, ZITADEL may create or link accounts based on external IdP information and configured linking options. The fuzzer MUST control whether automatic creation/linking is enabled when setting up the provider; otherwise identity merges are by configuration and not evidence of a collision bug.

For organization-scoped SAML/oidc broker tests, if organization-specific login settings override defaults, the authorization request MUST include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}. Without this scope, ZITADEL may use default instance settings and the wrong IdP/login policy, invalidating test conclusions.

Token exchange scope behavior is not simple intersection. ZITADEL documentation states scope can be entirely different from supplied tokens and can extend or decrease scope, subject to validation. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's actual scope/claims against documented validation outcomes rather than assuming automatic intersection semantics.

When introspecting a token, active=true additionally requires that the requesting client is part of the token audience. For verification and audience-binding tests, use an introspection client/application that is in the token audience; otherwise active=false is expected and is not proof of token invalidity.

For I2 freshness tests on JWT client assertions and JWT profile grants, the JWT iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Use template times such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for controls; otherwise failures may be due to malformed client authentication, not freshness enforcement.

ZITADEL does not support the OAuth 2.0 SAML 2.0 Profile grant and does not support Resource Owner Password Credentials. Do NOT generate SAML-bearer grant or password-grant token-endpoint tests; failures are by design and not security findings.

For I2 replay tests, stateless JWT replay is not the relevant SAML broker signal here. Focus on SAML assertion replay/OneTimeUse semantics and broker session outcomes; repeated use of ordinary OAuth access tokens is not documented as one-time and should not be flagged as a vulnerability by itself.
saml.source: attack pattern guidance cross-referenced with ZITADEL token docs

saml.constraint: The token endpoint accepts both Basic auth and body client_id/client_secret for some grants. For consistency in I3/I5 token-exchange and introspection tests, keep the client authentication method constant across control and attack requests; changing auth method can change failure mode and confound results.

When requesting user metadata or role claims for verification, the corresponding scopes must be requested explicitly (for example urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata or role scopes). Missing claims in userinfo/introspection without the scope are by design and must not be treated as authorization stripping or identity confusion.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths (e.g., 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...'). For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy. Both are needed before IdP login works.
